title: Legal and compliance
description: Identify the laws, contracts and licences the change touches and who must confirm them, without claiming compliance.
questions: Which laws, contracts or licences apply to this change, and who in the company confirms that reading?
Does the change alter what customers agreed to, what data is processed or who processes it?
Which record or notice must exist before release: register entry, impact assessment, contract amendment or licence notice?

sources.title: CNIL, Le règlement général sur la protection des données

specialists.title: Data protection counsel
specialists.focus: Map the personal data the change collects, uses or shares to its purpose, legal basis, retention and processors. Say which register or impact assessment needs an update.

specialists.title: Contracts counsel
specialists.focus: Compare the change with the customer terms, service levels and data processing agreements in force. Flag any new obligation, liability or notice period.

specialists.title: Licence compliance specialist
specialists.focus: Check the licences of new dependencies, assets and generated content against how the product is distributed, and record the notices to ship.

specialists.title: Regulatory specialist
specialists.focus: Identify the sector rules that apply to the customer or the product, such as finance, health, public sector or AI, and the reporting or testing they require.

evidence: Record of processing activities, data map or impact assessment covering the data involved.
Customer terms, order forms, service levels and data processing agreements that the change affects.
Dependency list with SPDX licence identifiers and the project's licence policy.
Written position of the legal or compliance owner for each regulation the project names.
challenge: Which customer could say the change breaks what they signed, and which clause would they cite?
Does a new dependency or asset carry a licence that conflicts with how the product is distributed?
Would the change require a notice to customers, a regulator or a data protection authority, and by when?
Are we treating an assumption about the law as a confirmed position?
decision_criteria: Proceed when the legal owner has confirmed the applicable obligations and the records they require exist or are scheduled before release.
Revise when a dependency licence, data flow or contract term calls for a change of scope or a notice.
Block when the change processes personal or regulated data without a documented basis, or ships a licence the policy forbids.
Record each open legal question with its owner instead of settling it with an assumption.
